articles.headline: What's the story with Scotland boss Pocognoli - is it time to go?
keyFacts: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli faces heavy criticism following a 4-0 defeat by Switzerland, adding pressure to the Scottish FA officials who appointed him.
Senior players Andy Robertson and John McGinn made critical post-match comments that raised doubts about the current coaching regime and team performance.
Pocognoli defended his team's attitude and argued the scoreline did not reflect the match, while fans and players expressed skepticism about his tactical system.
body: - Published
A few short months ago, Craig Mulholland, the Scottish FA's chief football officer, and Ian Maxwell, the association's chief executive, spoke about the worldwide search for a new Scotland head coach.
The data, the metrics, the cosmic input from the analytics company whose input was received at Hampden as if written on tablets of stone.
The process all pointed to Sebastien Pocognoli being their guy. They paraded him around Hampden, told everybody that loads of clubs were on his tail but that they won the chase.
They may, or may not, have mentioned the word 'coup' but that was certainly what their body language was telling you.
For coup, read boo, the sound surely reverberating around the Tartan Army right now after Monday's 4-0 defeat by Switzerland.
Some nonsense has been written about Pocognoli being on twice the salary that Steve Clarke was on, but whatever they're paying him, there's no value in it so far.

Money is a factor here. Clarke's three qualifications brought a rich bounty into the SFA's coffers, many millions even after deductions. That cash gave the association a little more opportunity to do some of the things they want to do in grassroots football.

A world where Scotland miss out on major championships and the financial windfalls that come with qualification is not a place they want to revisit. The next Euros looks like a gimme - almost harder not to qualify than qualify - but the sense of drift in this team is alarming and can't go on much longer.
Mulholland, Maxwell and let's throw SFA president Mike Mulraney into the mix, should be feeling mightily nervous.
What do players really think of the coach?

Most people understood that Pocognoli needed time, but implicit in that understanding was a need to see something developing under him, a burgeoning style of play, some positives here and there, a few signs that even though things might not be great today or tomorrow, they're inching in the right direction.

There's been none of that. Decent players look lost. Pocognoli's system has made Scotland a disjointed soft touch. Structural discipline collapses too often. Players charge forward and leave space in behind. He wants hard pressing and maximum intensity, but his players don't look capable of providing it.
In six games they have scored five goals - two from the penalty spot. Promises of jam tomorrow are not cutting it. People can see a team on the slide.
In Switzerland, there was a drubbing that piles the heat on the Belgian, on the people who appointed him and on the players, too.

If the chaos on the field wasn't a bad enough look for Pocognoli, then some of the words said in the wake of this objectionable 4-0 pummelling to a Switzerland B side playing in third gear only made things worse.
Andy Robertson, on the night he became Scotland's most capped player in history, delivered a damning riff that sounded strongly like a commentary on this coaching regime and this set of players.
In his stead, John McGinn did much the same thing. "You don't get time" was the gist. Who doesn't get time?

Robertson and McGinn didn't lay it on the line, but their thoughts resembled distress flares. These Scotland players can be overhyped, but they are better than some of the nonsense they dished up in St Gallen.
More than one former Scotland international reckoned they saw players not exactly busting a gut out there. These guys know the tell-tale signs.
Some private conversations between the SFA hierarchy and the senior operators in this team need to take place. What were they suggesting in the post-match? What are they really thinking?
An honesty session behind closed doors needs to take place long before the qualification campaign for the next Euros begins in March.
Pocognoli is heading down dead end... can he turn back?
Pocognoli comes across as a good person: open, communicative, passionate and hard-working.

He also appears stubborn in the way he sets up his team, a system that is so easily exploited by more experienced coaches, people like Switzerland boss Murat Yakin, who was missing a battalion of heavy hitters and yet still won this game at a canter.
Yakin started six players who had six caps or fewer to their name - three of them scored.
McGinn said later that Scotland were in this movie before in the early days of Clarke's tenure, mentioning the 4-0 loss to Russia in 2019 - four goals conceded in 27 minutes.

The difference between Clarke and Pocognoli is obvious. Clarke had vast experience and the nous to fix the problems. Pocognoli is a young coach with no such back story, no such track record in turning bad situations into good.
Pocognoli said later that people should look beyond the result, to the "attitude of the players" who were at times "brilliant, brave and on the front foot".

He argued that 4-0 wasn't a true reflection of the game, referring to the glaring misses by Lewis Ferguson and Scott McTominay. Scotland were 3-0 down at the time. He didn't think the loss had anything to do with a system or a lack of confidence or a lack of belief.
Not many fans were buying what he was selling. Listening to some of his players, you doubted that they were buying it either.

After the home loss to Slovenia, Robertson said his team had been "out-played" and "out-fought." There were some other comments made after the desperately stodgy 2-1 win over North Macedonia on Friday. On Monday, it cranked up another level.

McGinn was asked if he felt Scotland were on the right path. "Impossible for me to say yes," he replied. It was hard to listen to what the players were trying to say and conclude that everybody's on the same page in this set-up.

Intransigence is not a good characteristic for any manager. In recent times we've seen a few bosses at big clubs who were wedded to their principles. Russell Martin and Wilfried Nancy didn't last long at Rangers and Celtic.
To repeat Robertson's line, you don't get time.

Clarke had an instinctive understanding of that and pragmatism was his way of taking his team forward, difficult yard by difficult yard. Rigid idealism is not a sensible way to operate, but Pocognoli has gone down that road in his first six games.
It's a dead-end down there. He needs to turn back and find another way while he still can. If he still can.

articles.headline: James Comer launches bid for Kentucky governor
keyFacts: House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer launched his campaign for Kentucky governor on Monday night.
Comer stated that his policy priorities include reducing Kentucky's income tax to zero to attract businesses.
Kentucky's next gubernatorial primary election will occur in May 2027, followed by the general election in November 2027.
body: House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, R-Ky., is launching a campaign for governor on Monday night.

"Serving this state is a calling for me," Comer said during a tele-townhall. "Kentucky needs a leader whose policies will lead to growth and good-paying jobs. We need a leader whose priority will be to reduce taxes so Kentuckians can keep more of what they earn."

Comer teased a "major announcement" for Monday night earlier in the day. A source familiar with his plans told Fox News Digital it would be his long-awaited campaign to lead the commonwealth of Kentucky.
REDISTRICTING EFFORTS BLOW UP IN REPUBLICANS' FACES AMID HISTORIC HOUSE LOSSES
Comer spent the majority of his announcement fielding questions from Kentuckians on topics like education, small business, and high prices.
Among the policies he advocated for was reducing Kentucky's income tax to zero.

"We all talk about attracting new businesses and new industry to Kentucky," Comer said. "If we can get that existing income tax to zero, people are going to have more money to spend, and we're going to be able to attract more good-paying jobs to Kentucky, which will be able to keep our best and brightest in the state and help our state grow into the future."
Kentucky's gubernatorial election will take place in November 2027, with the primaries set for May of that year.
Gov. Andy Beshear, who is widely considered a potential contender for the Democratic presidential primary in 2028, is term-limited.
Comer ran for Kentucky governor in 2015 but narrowly lost the GOP primary to former Gov. Matt Bevin.
But this election cycle will likely see the House lawmaker enter as the frontrunner for his party's nomination.

Comer has served in the House of Representatives since November 2016, when he won a special election for Kentucky's 1st congressional district. Since then, his profile has skyrocketed as the top Republican on the House Oversight Committee for the better part of the last six years.
FOX NEWS VOTER POLL: HOW DEMOCRATS TOOK CONTROL OF THE SENATE

As committee chairman since Republicans took back the House majority in 2023, he's launched investigations into former President Joe Biden's use of autopen and the federal government's handling of Jeffrey Epstein's case, among others.
And despite Beshear's popularity as the state's two-term Democratic governor, Kentucky has historically been seen as a red state.
President Donald Trump defeated former Vice President Kamala Harris by roughly 30 points there in 2024. He beat former President Joe Biden there by 25.9% in 2020.

articles.headline: 'Avengers: Doomsday' Star Says He Was Lied to About His Next Big Role
keyFacts: Anthony Mackie stars as an FBI agent in the heist thriller series 12 12 12, which premiered on Apple TV on November 13.
Mackie stated in an interview that producers misled him by comparing the series to The Italian Job when it was actually different.
The first two episodes are currently streaming on Apple TV, with new episodes releasing weekly on Fridays through December 25.
body: Anthony Mackie’s Sam Wilson/Captain America will be leading the Avengers in Avengers: Doomsday, guiding Thor (Chris Hemsworth), Ant-Man (Paul Rudd), Shang-Chi (Simu Liu), and Falcon (Danny Ramirez) in the fight against Doctor Doom. But while Sam is getting a big promotion, Mackie said he was lied to about his next starring role.

Mackie plays FBI Special Agent Jack Strickland in 12 12 12, a heist thriller that premiered on Apple TV on Nov. 13. Jack’s partner was killed in a bank robbery gone wrong, and since then he’s been doggedly hunting the perpetrators, criminal mastermind Paul Galvin (Jamie Dornan), and his older brother and gunman Bobby Galvin (Jack Kesy). Jack tracked them to Zurich, where he believes they’re planning their next big job.

“This was pitched to me as ‘Imagine you in The Italian Job,’” Mackie told Polygon in a virtual interview. “I was like, ‘I’m in.’ It wasn’t that at all. They lied to me. I would have never taken this job.”

Mackie said that last part with a laugh, but he is bummed he doesn’t get to cruise around in a Mini Cooper, which is what he said makes The Italian Job his favorite heist movie. Series creators Dudi Appleton and Jim Keeble tried a different way to get Dornan into his role as the master thief, but the actor didn’t do the homework.

“Jim and Dudi sent me [a movie] that I didn’t watch,” he told Polygon. “It was French. That’s not fair. I did watch some of it. I can’t remember the name of it, but it felt removed from our show where it’s in Europe but all the main players were Americans. It felt to me not incredibly useful. I’m an Oceans 12 guy. Oceans 12, Oceans 13, and 14.”
Filming 12 12 12 was “headache-inducing”

12 12 12 takes its name from the FBI Principles of Crime, which hold that it takes 12 months to plan a high-value robbery, 12 hours to pull it off, and that law enforcement only has 12 days after the crime to successfully catch the culprits. Each episode of the show is split into three different timelines representing these periods, and filming was similarly scattered.

“It was all over the map,” Dornan said. “It was tough. You’d have days where you’d be doing scenes from different blocks, so you’d be working with different directors on one day. That’s problematic for everyone involved. That was just the situation because of the locations we were in, and the way the timelines jump around. It’s tricky. There’s a lot of needing to check in with people and track where your characters were at any given point and what had happened and what hadn’t happened. As you can imagine, it was quite headache-inducing a lot of the time. It was different from a lot of other jobs you do, which are a bit easier to track.”

Appleton and Keeble hope that structure will keep viewers on their toes, splitting more methodical planning with high-stakes action and chase scenes. The first two episodes of 12 12 12 are streaming on Apple TV now, with new episodes releasing weekly on Fridays through Dec. 25. The big Zurich heist takes place on Christmas Eve and the chase starts on Christmas Day, making it perfect holiday viewing.

body: Arion Kurtaj, a member of the Lapsus$ cybercrime group who leaked 90 videos of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022 and hacked other big companies, pleaded guilty on Monday, according to the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS).
Hacker behind 2022 GTA VI leaks pleads guilty
Arion Kurtaj leaked 90 videos of GTA VI years before its release.

Kurtaj, who is now 21, hacked BT/EE sometime between August and November 2021, and starting in early November of that year, the company “noted a marked increase in unauthorised SIM swaps of their customers mobile phones.” He was charged for those offenses and moved to a hotel for his “own protection” in September 2022, but “breached his bail conditions to carry out further hacks on major companies using a mobile phone, the hotel TV’s Wi-Fi and a firestick,” including hacks on Rockstar Games, Uber, and Revolut, the CPS says.
He was sentenced to life in a secure hospital in December 2023 because of his autism, but in January, Kurtaj was deemed fit for trial and moved to prison, the BBC reports.
Kurtaj is set to be sentenced on November 23rd. GTA VI will be released on November 19th.

articles.headline: Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months
keyFacts: AI cybersecurity startup Corma raised $125 million in Series A funding at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA.
Interest in Corma's AI products spiked after major security flaws were disclosed in PHP, Node.js, and LiteLLM on October 21.
Corma said it stands out from competitors by operating as a frontier AI research lab focused on protection.
body: Three months after introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corma has raised a $125 million Series A round at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA, the company said. Corma offers AI models and agents trained for cybersecurity defense. It has now raised a total of $185 million from backers, including Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Coatue.

The startup came out of stealth in August. Interest in its product skyrocketed after a series of security incidents sent chief information security officers scrambling on October 21 when a critical flaw was found in PHP, a popular web programming language. Another flaw was found in Node.js, the open source JavaScript runtime environment. Popular open source tool LiteLLM, a proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, also disclosed a security incident. Other incidents were disclosed that day, too. The day showcased the kind of onslaught on security that AI has enabled.

Corma isn’t the only company using AI to play defense. Other examples include Kevin Mandia’s new startup Armadin, as well as Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, and other established players, and too many other startups to count. Still, it’s a young market and a necessary one. Corma says it stands out from the crowd by being a frontier AI research lab focused on protection.

articles.headline: Pochettino: I’d tell Guardiola to ‘take it’ if he’s offered US coaching job
keyFacts: Outgoing US head coach Mauricio Pochettino stated he would advise Pep Guardiola to take the US coaching job if it is offered to him.
Pochettino noted that the US national team coaching position has gained more prestige in Europe following his tenure.
Pochettino recently departed the US role to become the manager of Manchester United.
body: Outgoing US head coach Mauricio Pochettino and former Manchester City head coach Pep Guardiola have a long, storied past. The two faced each other as players, when Guardiola was at Barcelona and Pochettino was making his name across town at Espanyol. They faced each other 22 times as managers in the Premier League and the two share a mutual respect – and intensity – when it comes to their approach to playing and coaching alike.

So when Guardiola visited Yankee Stadium in September to serve as New York City FC’s pre-match hype man before their rivalry match with Red Bull New York, Pochettino – in town anyways to scout the match – made it a point to sit with him during the game. He brought along his assistant coach and confidant Jesús Pérez, and US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson.
“You know what I noticed?” Pochettino asked, smiling as he recounted the story during a meeting with reporters on Monday. “[Guardiola had a] good relationship with JT.”

Back then, Pochettino didn’t seem to be going anywhere. Only a month earlier, he’d signed a four-year contract to guide the US through the 2030 World Cup. Guardiola was, and still is, in the middle of a year-long sabbatical from coaching. He remains the federation’s white whale, often mentioned in the same breath as the US job over the past decade-plus but just as quickly dismissed as a pipe dream.

Just three months after taking in that game at Yankee Stadium, Pochettino is on his way to Manchester United and Guardiola has once again found himself at the center of the rumor mill, with reports suggesting that he and US Soccer are set for exploratory talks.
On Monday, Pochettino was asked what he’d tell the Barcelona and Manchester City legend if he was asked for his opinion on the US job.

“Take it,” Pochettino said, flatly. “Why? Because it’s a perfect moment to arrive at the federation. Everything is on the right path, in the right direction. Of course, take it. Of course, you are going to find really good players, good people – the players can fit his style.”

Guardiola was one of many topics the Argentinian manager covered during the roundtable, which lasted about an hour. At times defiant, at times emotional and cycling through Spanish and English, Pochettino spoke of his potential legacy at US Soccer, what lies ahead for him at United and how he views soccer in America as a whole.
Quotes have been lightly edited and condensed for clarity.
On assessing players regardless of league level

However you assess his results, one of the inarguable successes of the Pochettino era are the relatively unheralded players whose status has risen over his tenure. The Argentine cited defender Alex Freeman and midfielder Sebastian Berhalter as two such examples, both of whom were playing in MLS when making their national team debuts under Pochettino and both now playing in Europe. Asked how he assesses players to add to the national team, and how he compares players across different leagues and playing styles, Pochettino insisted that the level of competition matters less than individual form.

“You need to project the individual player,” Pochettino said. “Because he’s playing well, the level is no issue. That player can be good, like Freeman, like Sebastian. That is the example, and I think that is so important. There is talent everywhere … This one is one of the things that we learn – all [of us], we were young and then we start to be a coach, no? That we cannot make a mistake [and] measure the level of the player because of the level of the league.”
On managing a club v managing a national team
With the US being his first international job, there were some doubts going in about how Pochettino would adapt to coaching without daily contact with his players and staff.

“I am ready [to return]. This is what I miss a little bit. I miss to be, every day, with something here,” Pochettino said. “Guardiola asked me when I was at the game, he said, ‘Oh, you don’t want to come back to the Premier League?’ I said, ‘No, I’m happy here.’ [He said] ‘Yeah, but you don’t miss, every day, to…’ I say, ‘A little bit, yes, because you think now today, and then we have December camp against Jamaica for the MLS [players in the pool]. But after, you need to wait [until] March. What do you do? You need to watch games, you need to travel – administrative things. That is nice, it’s good. But every day, to be involved: press conference, training, everything … this type of possibility, like with United, you say yes. I want that. I want to prove myself again.”
But what did Pochettino think of his maiden international job?

“I like and not like,” he said. “I like because it provides you the possibility to manage your time, to be busy, but at the same time, be free and to have some time with your family. Now, I have a grandchild, and [number] two is coming. You can share the life with your people. But now, ciao, because now is [gestures] tra-tra-tra-tra-tra. It’s impossible to spend time with the people you want.”
On the perceived status of the US coaching gig

In the grand scheme of international football, the US national team coaching job has never been close to the top of the list of most desirable destinations. Pochettino’s hire was seen as a possible sign that could be changing. Now, after nearly two years in the position, Pochettino believes it has.

“The vision from Europe, I promise it is completely different after the World Cup,” Pochettino said. “Now, being head coach of the USA is more prestigious. If Manchester United, or Real Madrid, or Barcelona is coming for the US coach, if you start to think about that, if you are another coach – maybe [Antonio] Conte, someone else, you say ‘oh, this is a great opportunity.’ [In my case], ‘Oh, Pochettino, from Chelsea he goes to the US? And now to Manchester United.’
On one thing he’d change about soccer in the United States

Pochettino has coached some of the most famous players and clubs in the world, giving him a unique perspective on how soccer has developed in the US. Pochettino stopped short of prescribing neat solutions to improve the sport, though.

“I think that business [and] the sport, is [done] in a holistic way. Everything is important, and you cannot pick one. You cannot change one [thing], and that can change everything,” he said. “I think it’s a little bit of everything that you need to change. If you adjust this, you need to adjust this. The balance of the thing changes if you touch here, that will force you to touch all the areas in soccer here, or in the world To find the good balance, no? A process of little by little, is all that we made in these last two years. I think it’s the beginning of [a process]. If that has continuity, it’s the beginning of the new soccer in the USA that can be.

“I think that is, for me, the beginning of the change for the future: that idea that the American player can be very good, can be very competitive. The talent is here; it’s so powerful in this country. I think that is why I feel proud. Maybe that was our job, because I don’t believe in coincidence. That has happened because something needed to happen. Now the tough job is done. Maybe now [the United job] is my reward because of this tough job.”

articles.headline: Jurgen Klopp inflicts brutal 121-year first on Netherlands as Germany top Nations League group
keyFacts: Germany defeated the Netherlands 5-0 in Berlin, with manager Jurgen Klopp securing top spot in their Nations League group.
The result marked the heaviest competitive defeat in the 121-year history of the Netherlands national team.
Despite the heavy defeat, the Netherlands still qualified for the Nations League quarter-finals by finishing second in the group.
body: Germany condemned the Netherlands to their biggest-ever competitive defeat as they thumped their rivals 5-0 .
In just his sixth game as national team boss, Jurgen Klopp inspired his team to an emphatic victory in Berlin to clinch top spot in their Nations League group.
Florian Wirtz made it three goals in two games as he hit a double against the Netherlands Getty
Five-star Germany
Heading into the clash in third place in Group A2, Germany needed to beat top of the table Holland to secure their spot in the quarter-finals and avoid a relegation play-off.
And there was no danger of the latter, as the hosts never looked back after Derry Scherhant opened the scoring just before half time.
Klopp’s side ran riot from there on in, with Liverpool’s Florian Wirtz grabbing a double either side of a Nico Schlotterbeck goal.
Brighton loanee Brajan Gruda rounded off the thumping win – scoring Germany’s fifth on 77 minutes after two assists earlier in the game.
The huge victory saw Germany not only qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals, their five-goal scoreline also saw them leapfrog the Netherlands into top spot on goal difference.
It marked the perfect night for Klopp’s men, who recorded their biggest-ever competitive win over Holland in their 118-year history.

Since their first-ever international game in 1908, Germany – then called West Germany – had previously beaten their rivals 7-0 in a friendly in 1959, which remains their greatest win in any form of the beautiful game over Holland.
Netherlands in new low
For Holland, their brutal defeat condemned manager Xavi to his first loss since his appointment in August – and it came in historic circumstances.
The result is their heaviest loss in a competitive match in the 121 years they have been playing international football – going back to 1905.
Never before had the European football giants lost by a five-goal margin in a competitive game.
Brajan Gruda and Wirtz ran riot against the Netherlands, with both stars getting on the scoresheet Getty
Xavi tasted defeat for the first time in international management against Germany Getty
The result represents a tough reality check for Xavi, who, prior to Monday night, had yet to lose as Holland boss.
The Spanish icon won three and drew two of his opening five games in charge, but came undone at the sixth attempt.
Fortunately for Holland though, their defeat to Germany didn’t cost them, as they still qualified for the Nations League knockouts via a second-place finish.
Having thumped Greece 7-0 in their last match, this result proved crucial as the top three nations in Group A2 finished level on points.
With Greece beating Serbia 1-0 on Monday night, they joined Germany and the Netherlands on 11 points.
But their heavy loss to the Netherlands meant they ended the Nations League campaign with an eight-goal inferior goal difference.
Jurgen Klopp celebrated his best win yet as Germany boss against Holland Getty
As a result, Greece will miss out on the quarter-finals, but avoided a relegation play-off thanks to finishing as the highest-ranked third-placed team in League A.
England could face Holland in last eight
With Germany clinching top spot, they will be seeded for the quarter-final draw, where they will be matched up against a side who finished second elsewhere.
Meanwhile the Netherlands are set to face a top-ranked nation – with England , France and Portugal/Denmark potential opponents.
Thomas Tuchel ‘s side pulled off a thrilling 3-2 win over world champions Spain to clinch first-place in Group A3.
And that now means the Three Lions will either face Holland, Belgium or Denmark/Norway in the last eight.

articles.headline: Trump closes an AI loophole
keyFacts: The Trump administration issued a rule restricting AI microchip exports to prevent China from accessing computing power through foreign data centers.
The action follows the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over ties to a firm renting compute to Chinese businesses.
The Commerce Department's new export rule is scheduled to take effect in 90 days.
body: President Donald Trump departs the White House on November 16, 2026, ahead of a trip to China and the Philippines. | Kent Nishimura/AFP via Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: The Trump administration is closing a global AI chip loophole that the Jensen Huang scandal put in the spotlight.
What’s changing? The Commerce Department is trying to make it harder for China to access top-of-the-line AI microchips like those made by Nvidia.
Currently, China is able to dodge export rules by renting computing power from third-country data centers, which can legally buy American-made chips that China can’t.

But under the rule issued Monday, which is set to take effect in 90 days, data centers in a handful of countries will face new export restrictions on chips — including a requirement that they perform “robust due diligence on their customers” to make sure that they aren’t evading an export ban.

What’s the context? Huang, who resigned from Nvidia last week, was brought down in part by his relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), an alleged Chinese spy ( kind of ) and an executive at a Singapore-based tech company, Megaspeed, that was renting compute to Chinese firms — exactly the kind of thing that the new rule aims to crack down on.

What’s the big picture? The Nvidia scandal is front and center. But under the hood, there’s also some Trump administration infighting going on. As a statement announcing the new rule notes, it was written not by the Commerce Department, which is issuing it, but by the Treasury Department and the National Security Council.

That’s conspicuous because Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has done his best to throw Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick under the bus for the scandal, saying that Lutnick’s department failed to restrict Megaspeed’s access to advanced AI chips sooner.

Where’s President Donald Trump in all this? As of Monday, off to China and the Philippines for a multiday trip that will feature a trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

For now, though, Trump is standing by Lutnick — and even by Jensen Huang, saying Monday that he “would certainly not mind” seeing him return as Nvidia CEO (the Nvidia board has already shut down the possibility).
And with that, it’s time to log off…

articles.headline: That 007 First Light theme song I didn't like is up for a Grammy Award
keyFacts: The 007 First Light theme song, composed by Joe Henson and Alexis Leon Smith and performed by Lana Del Rey, received a Grammy Award nomination in the Best Score Soundtrack For Videogames and Other Interactive Media category.
The track competes against four other game soundtracks, including scores from Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora - From the Ashes, Ghost of Yotei, Marvel's Wolverine, and Star Wars: Zero Company.
The 2027 Grammy Awards will take place on February 7, 2027, when the winner will be announced.
body: Remember that 007 First Light song Lana Del Rey surprised-dropped earlier this year that I said wasn't very good because, as I put it at the time, "it sounds like Bond karaoke"? Well anyway, it's up for a Grammy Award.
007 First light, composed by Joe Henson and Alexis Leon Smith, is in the running in the "Best Score Soundtrack For Videogames and Other Interactive Media" category, alongside four other contenders:
- Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora - From the Ashes, composer: Joe Paesano
- Ghost of Yotei, composer: Toma Otowa
- Marvel's Wolverine, composer : David Fleming
- Star Wars: Zero Company, composer: Gordy Haab

I haven't heard any of the other tracks in contention (in my defense, neither Ghost of Yotei nor Wolverine are available on PC, and I actively dislike Star Wars) but after listening to the 007 First Light theme again, and with more time to think about it, I will say this: My initial assessment was absolutely correct.

This is not a good Bond theme. Lana Del Rey may be tremendously talented, but that's lost in the all-consuming effort to hit all the notes without understanding what connects them: The end result is a pale imitation built out of a musical stereotype that's readily identifiable as someone trying really hard to do a Bond theme based on what they were told a Bond theme is supposed to sound like.

The Grammy Awards are a music industry award, not a game award, and that means some games that you might expect to be nominated are sometimes excluded: The rules for the videogame category state that "videogames that contain music but are not available as stand-alone audio streams/releases" are not eligible for consideration, for example. So if you don't see your favorite of the year in the list, that might be why.
The videogame soundtrack category is relatively new: The Grammy Awards only added it in 2022. Previous winners include:
- 2026 - Austin Wintory, Sword of the Sea
- 2025 - Winifred Phillips, Wizardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord
- 2024 - Stephen Barton And Gordy Haab, Star Wars Jedi: Survivor
- 2023 - Stephanie Economou, Assassin's Creed Valhalla: Dawn Of Ragnarok
Anyway, will being a bad Bond theme keep 007 First Light from winning a major music industry award? The 2027 Grammy Awards take place on February 7, 2027—we'll find out then.

articles.headline: 'I didn't know' - Price's controversial 145 checkout at Grand Slam explained
keyFacts: Gerwyn Price defeated Sebastian Bialecki 5-2 at the Grand Slam of Darts to reach the knockout stage.
Price was given a controversial leg win after the referee gave him incorrect remaining score information.
Price stated he was unaware of the scoring error until after the match ended.
body: Grand Slam of Darts: Gerwyn Price produces controversial 145 checkout en route to routine victory over Sebastian Bialecki

Gerwyn Price busts his score after hitting D20 - 10 over his required tally, but is given leg on account of having been given incorrect information by referee; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports up until the final on November 22
Monday 16 November 2026 23:17, UK
Gerwyn Price produced a controversial 145 checkout en route to a routine Grand Slam of Darts victory over Sebastian Bialecki on Monday night in Wolverhampton.
Price, the three-time champion in Wolverhampton, came through 5-2 against Poland's Bialecki to book his place in the knockout stage.
However, there was controversy during the final Group E match as Price hit a 145 finish when he had 135 remaining in the fourth leg of the match.

What happened?
'The Iceman' needed 135 to hold his throw, and he thought he had taken it out.
After hitting T19 he asked referee Charlie Corstophine what he had left and was told 88.
However, he actually needed 78.
With 88 in mind, Price incorrectly hit T16 and D20 to finish off the leg and was given the hold.
Of course, Price believed he had gone the correct route for what he needed and went on to set up a last 16 date with Ryan Searle.
What did Price say?
"I didn't know until I just walked in [to the press conference]," said Price. "I hit the first treble and I asked what I'd got left and he said 88.
"So I went treble 16 double top and he said game shot."
The Welshman admitted he was glad he didn't know or it would've weighed on his mind.
He added: "I know. I swear to God, I didn't even know until I came back here. I'm glad I didn't know because it probably would have played on my mind."
What does the PDC rulebook say?

6.4.6 Errors in arithmetic shall stand as detailed on the scoreboard unless corrected prior to the next throw of the player whose score is in error. Any error in the score can be corrected by the Referee at any time until Game Shot is called in
that leg.
6.4.7 If the incorrect score resulted in a leg win the result will stand unless corrected prior to the start of the next leg.
Price on new format
Both players went into the contest with one win each after beating Joe Hunt, which made it a straight shoot-out with only the group winners reaching the knockout stage this year.
Price had opened his week with a 5-3 win over Hunt on Saturday, racing into a 4-0 lead before Hunt won three legs in a row. Bialecki needed a deciding leg to beat Hunt 5-4 on Sunday.

The new format has already seen Ross Smith, Jonny Clayton and Luke Woodhouse suffer shock exits and Price said: "I prefer the old one [format], obviously. I've had some good memories here. You can slip up once, but in this one you can't.
"As you can see, a couple of good boys have gone, and they probably thought they'd have a second chance. But once you lose a game, that's it; you're gone."

articles.headline: Delete GTA 6 For A Chance To Win Another Game
keyFacts: Devolver Digital is offering a chance to win their game Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed to people who delete their GTA 6 pre-load.
Participants can also enter the contest by sending a video of themselves biting into a raw onion to the publisher.
Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed releases on November 19, the same day as the highly anticipated GTA 6.
body: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases this week. The game looms so large that other companies are using it to market their own games, including Devolver Digital.

The publisher has announced that people can enter for a chance to win their upcoming game, Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, by reposting the message below with a video of themselves deleting their GTA 6 pre-load. Of course, anyone who deletes their pre-load can install it again, though it might take some time given the game is 212GB .
https://twitter.com/devolverdigital/status/2122404424983146756

The lucky winners will get a Steam key for Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed , not a console code since the game's console plans haven't been confirmed yet, so that's something to keep in mind if you're taking part in this campaign.
If you were never planning to buy GTA 6 but still want to enter the contest, you can send a video of yourself biting into a raw onion to Devolver.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qio_Ru2_McU

Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, priced at $5 (or $3.74 until launch), releases on November 19, which is the same day that GTA 6 comes out. Reslimed was originally prototyped as a retro-style 2D platformer for Game Boy Color and was pitched by developer Doinksoft before the GTA 6 conversation really ramped up.

"There is no doubt GTA 6 will have the spotlight before, during, and after November 19, but it’s not for everyone, or releasing on Steam the same day, so we figure there’s a bit of counter-programming that may work in Volvy’s favor," Devolver told Kotaku .

articles.headline: Star Wars: Galactic Racer is getting much-requested split-screen multiplayer and new mode in 2027
keyFacts: Developer Fuse Games announced that Star Wars: Galactic Racer will add local split-screen multiplayer in early 2027.
The new Free Play mode will allow players to customize vehicles, characters, tracks, and planets for local racing with up to four players.
This update addresses fan requests for same-room multiplayer, which is currently unavailable in the game's existing online modes.
body: The surprisingly awesome arcade podracing game Star Wars: Galactic Racer is getting split-screen multiplayer next year after loud fan requests, developer Fuse Games has announced.

Split-screen racing comes as part of an entirely new mode called Free Play that'll also allow players to mix and match vehicles, characters, tracks and planets in a galaxy far, far away. So, maybe don't expect to bring friends into the game's vast, pre-existing suite of modes just yet.

"We heard you," the studio wrote on social media. "Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to Star Wars: Galactic Racer. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action."

We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at @Fuse_Games has been working hard to bring a brand new mode, Free Play, to STAR WARS: Galactic Racer™. This new mode will allow you to choose your vehicle, character, planet, and race track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local split-screen action.
— STAR WARS: Galactic Racer™ (@SWGalacticRacer) November 16, 2026

Galactic Racer already has a pretty good selection of online multiplayer modes, like the 12-player speeder races and 8-player podracing tours, but there's currently no way to play with your mates in the same room.

Chris Donlan loved the thrilling racing game for mixing the best bits of Star Wars and Burnout - Fuse Games does have plenty of old Criterion DNA, mind you. "It's new games, with Roguelite choices and endless unlockables, and it's also old games, with cruel and ingenious courses where everything can be lost in an instant. It's a Galaxy Far, Far Away, and it's also Paradise City," he wrote in Eurogamer's five-star review.

With Galactic Racer and Zero Company under its belt, Lucasfilm Games said it's now "more flexible" about which developers it accepts pitches from. Hopefully, that'll lead to even more interesting games set in Star Wars' ultra flexible world.

articles.headline: Trump backs return of ex-Nvidia boss after 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign launched
keyFacts: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after extra-marital affairs emerged, prompting tech leaders and Donald Trump to support his return.
One affair involved a woman suspected of spying for China, which raised national security questions and erased billions in Nvidia's value.
Huang agreed to testify before Congress, while Nvidia's board conducts an internal investigation and is reportedly not considering reappointing him.
body: - Published
US President Donald Trump has said he "would certainly not mind" seeing Jensen Huang handed back his job as allies of the former Nvidia chief executive called for him to be reinstated.
Huang resigned as boss of the AI chip giant last week after the emergence of two affairs, one of which was with a woman suspected of spying for China and another allegedly with one of his employees.
It has created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms, which is a key part of the AI industry and its huge expansion.
But now fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have backed a campaign to get Nvidia's board to "Bring Jensen Back".
The pair were among more than 175,000 signatories of an open letter calling for the board to reinstate Huang while an ongoing internal probe is conducted.
President Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back.
"I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters as he left the White House.

The president's comments come after the "Stand with Jensen" campaign group, which claims to be made up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, demanded the return of the former chief executive.
They expressed concerns the ex-Nvidia boss "was removed without meaningful due process".
Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy.
However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him.

The scandal-hit tech boss is now discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times, external, though the publication reported Nvidia's board is not considering reappointing him.
A representative for Jensen Huang declined to comment on the report. The BBC has contacted Nvidia for comment.
The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House.
President Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal broke out, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy".
Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary, Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company.

The scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy.
It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.
'China plays games with us, so we play games with China'
On Monday, Trump said he did not know whether the women Huang had an affair with was a spy for China.
"They say she's a spy. I don't know that she was a spy at all. I mean, I really don't, I don't know that." he said.

The Trump administration issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres on Monday, which allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train AI models ahead of Trump's meeting with China President Xi Jingping.

The new rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to cut down on them being illegally diverted.
Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair.
Trump said he did not think Huang had put national security at risk. "You know, China plays games with us. So we play games with China," he said.
The BBC understands that the likelihood of Huang being reinstated is low while Nvidia's internal investigations are ongoing.
The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump.
'A handshake with Jensen'
Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation.
"Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," he posted on X., external
"Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."
Fellow tech boss Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, sidestepped the question of Huang returning to Nvidia at a conference, saying: "I don't think I know enough to answer that question."
But Altman, who himself was reinstated to his job after being fired back in 2023, said Huang was a "hero of mine".
Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at the company's helm.
Hundreds of billions of pounds have been wiped off the firm's stock market value in recent days, but it is still worth some $3.87 trillion. Its share price was down in early Monday trading.

In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang".

Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation.
For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday.

But now fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have backed a campaign to get Nvidia's board to "Bring Jensen Back".
The pair were among more than 175,000 signatories of an open letter calling for the board to reinstate Huang while an ongoing internal probe is conducted.
President Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back.
"I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters as he left the White House.

The president's comments come after the "Stand with Jensen" campaign group, which claims to be made up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, demanded the return of the former chief executive.
They expressed concerns the ex-Nvidia boss "was removed without meaningful due process".
Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy.
However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him.

The scandal-hit tech boss is now discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times, external, though the publication reported Nvidia's board is not considering reappointing him.
A representative for Jensen Huang declined to comment on the report. The BBC has contacted Nvidia for comment.
The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House.
President Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal broke out, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy".
Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary, Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company.

The scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy.
It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.
'China plays games with us, so we play games with China'
On Monday, Trump said he did not know whether the women Huang had an affair with was a spy for China.
"They say she's a spy. I don't know that she was a spy at all. I mean, I really don't, I don't know that." he said.

The Trump administration issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres on Monday, which allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train AI models ahead of Trump's meeting with China President Xi Jingping.

The new rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to cut down on them being illegally diverted.
Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair.
Trump said he did not think Huang had put national security at risk. "You know, China plays games with us. So we play games with China," he said.
The BBC understands that the likelihood of Huang being reinstated is low while Nvidia's internal investigations are ongoing.
The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump.
'A handshake with Jensen'
Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation.
"Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," he posted on X., external
"Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."
Fellow tech boss Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, sidestepped the question of Huang returning to Nvidia at a conference, saying: "I don't think I know enough to answer that question."
But Altman, who himself was reinstated to his job after being fired back in 2023, said Huang was a "hero of mine".
Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at the company's helm.
Hundreds of billions of pounds have been wiped off the firm's stock market value in recent days, but it is still worth some $3.87 trillion. Its share price was down in early Monday trading.

In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang".

Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation.
For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday.

As Donald Trump and tech leaders clamor for his return as Nvidia’s CEO, the company’s board of directors is reportedly not considering bringing back Jensen Huang.

The board is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back, CNBC reports this morning, citing a person familiar with the matter. Reuters hears the same, also citing a person familiar.

The secluded island of Ni‘ihau has long been a Republican stronghold in deep blue Hawai‘i. Ni‘ihauans have an unusual tendency to unanimously support conservative candidates, like in 2020, when all 43 Ni‘ihauan voters cast their ballots for Donald Trump.

This has been the case since as far back as the early 1900s, when Ni‘ihau’s ballots were sometimes relayed to the neighboring island of Kaua‘i via carrier pigeon. The headline of one characteristic 1939 Honolulu Star Bulletin article reads – “Ni‘ihau Casts 59 Votes All For GOP as Usual.” Bush beat Kerry 39-0, Reagan beat Carter 56-1, and Nixon beat Kennedy 99-0.

But this month, for the first time in recent memory, the island backed a Democrat for governor, casting 14 of their 21 votes for governor Josh Green and lieutenant governor Derek Kawakami. Has Ni‘ihau been caught up in the blue tsunami?
Donald Trump’s efforts to blame Friday’s four-hour nationwide flight stoppage – and the resulting travel chaos – on Democrats are “absurd”, an incoming Democratic member of Congress said yesterday.

The president remained largely silent and out of public view as air travel shut down on Friday, but yesterday he emerged to issue a series of posts blaming the incident on the Biden administration, despite Trump being in office for the last two years in which time Republicans have had control of Congress. He has continued this blame game today (see our earlier post).
Dan Koh, a US House representative-elect from Massachusetts and former Biden administration official, blasted the effort to cast aside blame.

“It’s kind of revisionist history – you might as well start blaming Ronald Reagan for the FAA strike in the 80s as part of this, too,” he said yesterday during an appearance on MS NOW’s The Weekend. “It’s absurd.”

Koh said Joe Bidensecured “historic funding not only to the FAA but over a trillion dollars of infrastructure money” between Trump’s two presidencies. But, Koh added, “a lot of it … Donald Trump has reversed on the grounds of it being too woke”, invoking a term that those on the political right use to refer to things they perceive to be overly leftist.

The congressman-elect said he talks frequently with mayors and city council members in his district about “all this money that would help them with upgrades to transportation including flights” – but “they don’t even know if they’re going to get any more because the [Trump] administration has not even gotten back to them on the status.” He added:
This is the reality: Donald Trump likes to say it’s Biden’s fault, but it’s actually his policies that are stopping the funding from hitting the towns and cities.

Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, announced on Monday that he was disbanding a controversial city police unit that has faced criticism over the years from civil rights groups who have accused the unit of using excessive force and unduly aggressive tactics against protesters.

In a video released on Monday morning, Mamdani said the move stemmed from a campaign pledge he made to disband the New York City police department’s strategic response group (SRG). “Today, we are keeping that promise,” Mamdani said in the video.

An accompanying joint statement from Mamdani and NYPD commissioner Jessica Tisch said the overhaul would “transform how the city prepares for and responds to protests, placing communication, de-escalation and civilian coordination at the center of our approach, while protecting New Yorkers’ constitutional right to protest”.

Along with eliminating the SRG, which was founded in 2015 ostensibly to focus on counter-terrorism, Mamdani and Tisch’s statement also said that the city planned to establish a “first-of-its-kind, civilian-led Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division (CDDD)” within the mayor’s office of community safety.
That division will not have weapons or arrest powers, unlike the SRG, according to the announcement.

The city will also establish what they described as a “specialized dialogue team” that will be known as the “First Amendment Support Team” (Fast) within the NYPD’s community affairs bureau, Mamdani and Tisch’s statement said. The creation of Fast is meant to “improve the NYPD’s protest response”, and it will consist of 30 uniformed officers trained in communication and de-escalation, the mayor and police commissioner said.

Trump continues to blame Biden administration for nationwide ground stop despite two years in office and Republican control of Congress
Trump also continued to shift responsibility to Joe Biden administration for the national ground stop over the weekend, that saw thousands of flights.

This is just the second nationwide ground stop of all departures since the 9/11 attacks. The previous one came in January 2023, when the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) paused all domestic departures for less than two hours.

“I hate to blame anybody, but the Biden administration hooked up a lot of copper into glass, and if you know anything about electrical engineering you cannot hook up copper into glass,” Trump claimed. “A lot of money was wasted, but the equipment is very old, in some cases more than 50 years old, and we essentially want to blow it up and put a new one in, and we can do it simultaneously with very little trouble. So that’s what we’re doing, but we need the funding to get it done. But essentially what you saw on Friday was very, very old equipment that had a heart attack.”

Trump’s claims comes after Congress, under Republican control, passed a $12.5bn air traffic control package in 2025, as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The president, however, appeared convinced that lawmakers would be now more willing to allocate more funding to upgrade the systems. “I think the one good thing that comes out of it I’m sure Congress now will give us the money,” he told reporters today.
Over the weekend, Sean Duffy, the transportation secretary, said in an interview with ABC News that the existing funding did not provide money for “a new architecture for telecom”.

“I don’t have any money given by Congress to build a new software system to manage the airspace. They’re very specific on how we spend the 12.5 and none of the money goes to this telecom that I have to build,” he said.
However, the top House Democrats on two key transportation and aviation committees said in a statement that, as of now, $8bn remains unobligated and $11bn is unspent.
Today, Trump also scolded a reporter for questioning why he has spent considerable time devoting energy and resources to White House renovation projects, instead of the FAA upgrades.

“You’re so pathetic,” he said. “I have a responsibility to make sure the symbol of our country is in decent shape, and it takes me 10 minutes a day. Very little time … That building, if you looked a year ago when I came back, was in horrible condition.”
Trump says it 'isn't a bad idea' for Huang to be reinstated as Nvidia CEO
Graeme Wearden
Donald Trump said today that he would not mind seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as the chief executive officer of Nvidia.
Trump is speaking to reporters now, ahead of his trip to Manila to attend the Asean summit.
The president added that the suggestion that Huang could return to Nvidia is not a bad idea. He says the ex-CEO has learned a lesson, and denies that national security has been put at risk.
“I think having Jensen go back – a lot of people are asking Jensen - they think Jensen should go back. That certainly isn’t a bad idea,” the president said.
That’s quite an intervention, as an open letter circulates calling for the chip giant to reinstate Huang.

Elon Musk and a host of other tech bosses have called for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia, amid reports the former chief executive is already plotting a return to the chip company just four days after his resignation.
An open letter that has more than 165,000 signatories demands that the company’s board members “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts”.

Huang’s resignation on Thursday ended a 33-year run at the helm of the AI company he co-founded, after reports he had at least two extramarital affairs, one with a woman accused of spying for China and another with a subordinate.

According to the Financial Times, Huang has discussed a possible return to the company with people close to him. One Huang ally told the paper they were putting together a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia CEO’s return and would try to garner support from the White House.
“Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,” the person said, adding that the efforts had Huang’s support.

According to the state’s election laws, if no candidate manages to cross the 50% threshold, that triggers a ranked-choice runoff where the candidate with fewest votes is eliminated but their vote goes to their second choice (which they mark on their ballot). This happens in rounds until the candidate with the most votes wins.
Donald Trump will begin his day in Washington, before traveling to Manila, Philippines, for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit.

Trump’s first order or business will be his first meeting with the “Quad” alliance since he returned to the White House last year. This group includes Indian prime minister Narendra Modi, Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese, and Sanae Takaichi, the Japanese prime minister.
Then, later this week, Trump will take part in the first trilateral summit between China’s Xi Jinping and Russian president Vladimir Putin.

Peltola inches closer to finish line in last US Senate race of midterm elections
Democrat Mary Peltola is leading Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan in the nail-biting race for US Senate in Alaska.
With 97% of the ballots counted, Peltola – a former congresswoman – has 49.9% of the vote and only needs more than 50% to win.
At present, Sullivan only has 46% of the vote. This would be the Democrats’ ninth flip of the midterms cycle and the first time the party has won a US Senate since 2009.

On Sunday Trump continued to blast Ana Reyes, the federal judge appointed by Joe Biden, who has temporarily blocked construction on the historic Washington public golf course that the president wants to turn it into a championship-level course.

“Why would a judge want to delay taking a terrible and very unsafe golf course, one that is mocked all over D.C.(and far beyond!), instead of quickly turning it into a great and admired one?” Trump wrote on Truth Social, noting that his administration plans to appeal the ruling. “Time is of the essence, or golf seasons, jobs, prestige, and much money, will be lost!”
US air travel was slowly returning to normal on Monday after three days of widespread disruption following an extraordinary no-takeoff order issued by US aviation authorities.

The ground stop issued on Friday afternoon was only the second time such a directive had been issued nationwide in the busy US airspace since planes were grounded following the 9/11 attacks and was blamed by the Trump administration on a faulty upgrade to communications equipment.
On Monday morning, more than 250 US-related flights – those traveling within, into or out of the United States – scheduled for the same day were cancelled, according to industry tracker FlightAware.
That marked a dramatic shift from the more than 2,300 flights cancelled on Sunday.
There were delays to more than 700 US-related flights scheduled for Monday, compared to more than 10,000 the previous day, AFP reported.
Elizabeth Warren just the latest Democrat to receive letter from DoJ
A progressive and onetime presidential candidate, Senator Elizabeth Warren is a vocal Wall Street critic and has repeatedly condemned the Trump administration and its policies.
She is the top Democrat on the Senate banking committee, and is widely expected to become chair when Democrats take over Congress, Reuters reported.
The US Department of Justice on Sunday warned her of potential “significant legal consequences” if she fails to preserve records related to investigations into Donald Trump.

Aaron Reitz’s letter to Warren cited her statements on investigating corporate leaders. “The context sends a strong smoke signal: you intend to target private individuals close to president Trump,” he wrote.

Other Democratic lawmakers who have received similar letters include Senators Richard Blumenthal and Elissa Slotkin as well as Representative Robert Garcia, who is in line to lead the House oversight committee.
Political experts and Trump’s opponents have raised concerns about efforts by the Republican president and his administration to target their own critics and political opponents.
Trump to embark on Asia trip in apparent foreign policy push before end of term
Robert Tait

Donald Trump is embarking on his first overseas trip since his Republican party’s thumping midterm repudiation by US voters, in what may herald a renewed focus on foreign policy for the remainder of his presidency.

The US president will meet his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, for their first trilateral summit, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) forum in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. Before that, he will land in Manila in the Philippines on Tuesday for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit.
At the Asean summit, Trump is expected to sign a trade agreement with Thailand, push deals with other countries and lobby fellow leaders to favour the US over China on artificial intelligence.
He will also take part in the first leaders’ meeting of the Quad partnership – consisting of the US, Japan, India and Australia – since he returned to the White House in January 2025.

White House officials said the president would be accompanied to Apec by Elon Musk, the Tesla and SpaceX entrepreneur who spent almost $500m (£380m) unsuccessfully supporting Republican candidates in this month’s midterms. The reason for Musk’s presence has not been explained.

The China leg of the trip will take place amid the continuing fallout from the Nvidia spying scandal, which prompted the company’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, to resign amid revelations he had had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Trump is under pressure to raise the matter with Xi when they hold a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of Apec.

The US president has said he does not plan to bring up the subject; administration officials insist he will not do so and that the meeting will be dedicated to implementing a trade agreement between the two superpowers.

Democratic US senator Chris Van Hollen on Sunday escalated his bid to lead his party’s incoming Senate majority rather than Chuck Schumer, asserting that he has a path to victory amid a dedicated campaign that includes a series of television appearances.

Van Hollen, a Maryland progressive, appeared on Sunday on CNN, ABC and Fox News as he continues to make his case for why his peers in the Senate should reject Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus for nearly a decade.
On CNN’s State of the Union, he reaffirmed that he believes he has a path to victory, citing support and a widespread openness to change within the Senate Democratic caucus.

“This really is a response to the call of the voters, who clearly rejected Donald Trump and his awful policies, but they haven’t fully hired the Democrats,” Van Hollen said, alluding to how the US president’s Republican party lost control of Congress during the 3 November midterm elections.
“They’ve given us a chance, and I think we need to earn their trust. And I think that begins by not going back to business as usual.”

Van Hollen criticized reports that Schumer’s team may move the Senate caucus leadership election date earlier than 1 December. He contended that the caucus should have a debate about the group’s direction as the Democrats assume control of Congress in January for the second half of Trump’s second presidency.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, the likely incoming chair of the Senate banking committee, was warned by the US Department of Justice of potential “significant legal consequences” if she fails to preserve records related to investigations into president Donald Trump.
It is the latest warning sent by the justice department to congressional Democrats about their potential plans to investigate the administration or Trump associates, Reuters reported.

Trump last week ordered the department to look into Democratic lawmakers for “threatening” people, and US attorney-general Todd Blanche subsequently indicated that his agency was prepared to battle congressional Democrats.

In a letter to Warren, US attorney Aaron Reitz in Houston told the Massachusetts Democrat she appeared “eager to wield your future gavel like a tomahawk, hunting for the scalps of president Trump’s private associates”.
Reitz told her to preserve materials “relevant to your intent to weaponize congressional investigations and deprive citizens of their core constitutional rights”.

Notices to preserve records can presage investigations. Warren’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Reitz shared the letter on social media and Trump reposted it to his Truth Social account several hours later.

Warren and other Democrats have signaled that when their party takes control of Congress in January, they plan to investigate large corporations, White House chief of staff Stephen Miller and Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, among others.

Colom, while being interviewed by CNN host Dana Bash on Sunday, alluded to various campaign promises made by Trump – including lowering consumer prices, halting the seemingly endless wars waged under other presidential administrations, and fully releasing files related to the prosecution of Jeffrey Epstein, the late accused sex trafficker whose social circle encompassed the US and global elite.
